first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this, so I read it properly on the iPad, top to bottom. The opening is clear enough and I like that it doesn't gush. But the first few screens are about rain gauges and weather stations, and what I actually want to know is who's looking after the money and whether Mum can manage the trip. I only got to that near the bottom.

journey.section: How we chose these Oceania destinations
journey.quote: The stations differ in period and in what counts as a rain day: Nadi covers 1961 to 1990, Apia 1971 to 2000 and Hamilton Island 2002 to 2026, so read each figure on its own terms.
journey.reaction: I read this twice and I'm still not sure what I'm meant to do with it. It reads like a footnote for a meteorologist, not something for the mother of the bride.

journey.quote: It also reports a National State of Disaster over worsening El Niño conditions, with possible water rationing.
journey.reaction: I'm glad they told me, it's honest. But it worries me. Water rationing with my mother and an aunt in their eighties? I'd want someone to tell me straight what that means for guests.

journey.quote: Can the covered ceremony space and the cyclone postponement terms be written into our contract?
journey.reaction: Good. Someone's thinking about contracts. That's the sort of question I'd ask myself.

journey.quote: Check with the destination's authorities, starting with Fiji's High Commission, or plan a symbolic ceremony in Fiji and marry legally at home.
journey.reaction: This line, or something like it, comes up again and again. Each time I think: isn't that what I'd be paying you for? I'd rather hear that the Advisor sorts this out than be told to ring a High Commission.

journey.quote: Should flights be suspended before the wedding, how are the date and our deposits handled?
journey.reaction: Finally, the word deposits. This is exactly my worry. But it's only a question for the venue. Nobody says whether the deposit is protected or who chases it if things go wrong.

journey.quote: Expect a request for a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) or Certificat de Célibat and a Certificat de Coutume, and possibly apostilles on Australian documents.
journey.reaction: French paperwork and apostilles. This is my fear of contracts in another language in a nutshell. Useful to know, but I'd cross Tahiti off unless someone handles it for us.

journey.quote: reports a dengue outbreak ongoing since 2025.
journey.reaction: Again, honest and I appreciate it. It's the sort of thing my husband will ask about, so I'm glad it's here.

journey.quote: Closer to home, the reef islands offer warm water and Australian law, with no passport needed.
journey.reaction: Now that's reassuring. Australian law, no foreign contracts. For the older relatives this might be the sensible option, and I'll point it out to my daughter.

journey.quote: This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Fair enough. It tells me they're being careful, not making promises.

journey.quote: Ask each venue how guests with limited mobility reach the ceremony across sand or by boat, where the nearest medical care is, and whether a Sunday rule touches your wedding weekend.
journey.reaction: At last, the older guests. This is the part I care about most and it's one sentence near the end. No mention of travel insurance at all.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One person responsible, including payments. That's what I want to hear. I'd like to know their name and whether I can speak to them on the phone.

journey.section: Plan your Oceania wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Advisor quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: This is the best sentence on the page for me. AUD and in writing. I'd have liked to see it much higher up.

unanswered_questions: Is our deposit protected if an overseas venue or supplier lets us down, and who chases it?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am island time during the wedding week?
Can I speak to the Advisor on the phone before anything is booked, and will I know their name?
Are the venue contracts in English, and in what currency are they written, even if your quote is in AUD?
What travel insurance should older guests have, and do you help check it?
Can someone help us find a venue where a guest with a walking frame can get to the ceremony and reception?
How much is the Advisor's fee, roughly, and when is it paid?

turn_offs_found.quote: The stations differ in period and in what counts as a rain day: Nadi covers 1961 to 1990, Apia 1971 to 2000 and Hamilton Island 2002 to 2026, so read each figure on its own terms.
turn_offs_found.why: Technical and dry. It's not slang, but it makes me feel the page is written for someone else.

turn_offs_found.quote: Check with the destination's authorities, or plan a symbolic ceremony.
turn_offs_found.why: Repeated for several countries. It leaves me feeling nobody is responsible for the legal side, which is one of my turn-offs.

would_share_with: My husband, with the deposit and insurance questions written underneath
My daughter, pointing at the Whitsundays section for the older relatives

cta_reaction.quote: Tell [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=oceania-wedding-destinations&utm_content=closing) which islands are on your list, your month and how many guests are travelling.
cta_reaction.why: The AUD quote and written fee make me willing. But I'd want to know it leads to a phone call with a real person, not a form, and I'd want to mention my mother's mobility up front. I'd probably leave it to my daughter to click and ask her to get someone to ring me.

top_3_changes: In the Fiji venue questions, add the deposit to the contract question. Old: "Can the covered ceremony space and the cyclone postponement terms be written into our contract?" New: "Can the covered ceremony space, the cyclone postponement terms and what happens to our deposit be written into our contract?"

Give older guests more than one line. Old: "Ask each venue how guests with limited mobility reach the ceremony across sand or by boat, where the nearest medical care is, and whether a Sunday rule touches your wedding weekend." New: "Ask each venue how guests with limited mobility, including anyone using a walking frame or wheelchair, reach the ceremony across sand or by boat, where the nearest medical care is, and whether a Sunday rule touches your wedding weekend. Ask older guests to check that their travel insurance covers their health and their travel dates."

Invite the practical detail in the closing ask. Old: "which islands are on your list, your month and how many guests are travelling." New: "which islands are on your list, your month, how many guests are travelling, and whether any older guests need help with mobility or medical care."
